method.value: Background subtraction between the two exposures, flat-fielding, recentring, bad-pixel removal and high-pass spatial filtering; final image is the mean of the recentred frames

evidence.quote: The raw data, two exposures per star, were background subtracted one from the other, flat-fielded, then recentered to have the target in the center of the detector.
Finally, in order to reduce the effects of atmospheric turbulences on the images, a high-pass spatial filter has been used.

evidence.quote: For each star we took two exposures (of 200 NDIT[^3] each), where the star fell in two different quadrants of the detector to permit a quasi-simultaneous subtraction of the background.

For each binary system we calculated the position of the companion and its flux ratio with respect to the primary.

method.value: 2MASS K magnitudes converted to L' with spectral-type colours, corrected for K-band extinction, converted to mass with AMES-COND models

evidence.quote: To calculate the mass we used the 2MASS K band photometry, available for all the primaries, then we derived the L$^{\prime}$ magnitude using the color for the different spectral types as in (cite: 2015A&A...574A..78S).
To convert the absolute magnitude into mass we used the AMES-COND evolutionary models by (cite: 2001ApJ...556..357A).

analysis_steps.goal: Convert mm flux to disc dust mass

method.value: Dust mass in Earth masses = millimeter flux in mJy multiplied by 0.58

evidence.quote: we multiplied the millimeter flux in mJy (cite: 2019ApJ...875L...9W) by 0.58

assumptions.value: Distance of 140 pc and dust temperature of 20 K

analysis_steps.goal: Compare dust mass distributions by multiplicity category

method.value: Sample split into five categories; cumulative distributions with Kaplan-Meier product estimator to handle non-detections

evidence.quote: we divided the sample into five categories: single objects, multiple discs where all components are detected and resolved by ALMA, multiple systems unresolved by ALMA, binaries where one or both the components are not detected in the mm, and binaries without IR excess.
For non-detections, we used the Kaplan-Meier (KM) product estimator.

assumptions.value: For resolved multiple discs the system mass is the sum of the components; per-star mass is the system mass divided by two

evidence.quote: In the case where each component is resolved, the total mass of the system is the sum of the mass of each component.
In the latter case, the total disc dust mass are divided by two.

analysis_steps.goal: Relate disc mass and size to projected separation

evidence.quote: show the correlation between the dust mass and the size of the disc as a function of the projected separation between the primary and the companion.

results_numeric.quantity: NIR-ODISEA stars observed in NIR AO for the first time

evidence.quote: The NIR-ODISEA survey consists of 147 stars observed in NIR AO imaging for the first time
Nine companions are in the sub-stellar regime (30-50 M$_{\mathrm{Jup}}$).
One object, GY92 367 b (C5_090b), is in the planetary regime (14 M$_{\mathrm{Jup}}$)
The total number of multiple systems of ODISEA is 43, so the occurrence rate is 18% (43/236).

results_numeric.quantity: Occurrence rate of visual binaries among diskless Ophiuchus stars

evidence.quote: the ocurrence rate of visual binaries in the diskless stars in Ophiuchus is 30$\%$

results_numeric.quantity: Maximum disc dust mass in multiple systems vs single stars

evidence.quote: Discs in multiple systems reach a maximum total dust mass of $\sim$ 50 M$_{\oplus}$, while discs in single stars can reach a dust mass of 200 M$_{\oplus}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Projected separation above which discs with masses above 10 Earth masses are found

evidence.quote: Discs with masses above 10 M$_{\oplus}$ are found only around binaries with projected separations larger than $\sim$ 110 au.

results_numeric.quantity: NACO and NIRC2 contrast limits (companion flux fainter than primary)

evidence.quote: in general companions with a flux 50 times fainter than the primary are detected.
allowing the detection of companions 100 times fainter than the primary.

findings_qualitative.value: Discs around primaries tend to be more massive than discs around companions

evidence.quote: Primary stars tend to have more massive discs than secondaries.

findings_qualitative.value: Effect of visual binaries is weak in the general disc population because most Ophiuchus discs are small and low-mass

evidence.quote: However, since most discs in Ophiuchus are very small and low-mass, the effect of visual binaries is relatively weak in the general disc population.

claims.hypothesis: Stellar companions limit the maximum dust mass of circumstellar discs
claims.experiment: NIR AO multiplicity survey of ODISEA targets combined with ALMA 1.3 mm fluxes converted to dust masses, with Kaplan-Meier cumulative distributions by category
claims.result: Single and multiple systems have similar distributions up to 50 Earth masses; masses up to 200 Earth masses occur only around single stars
claims.finding: Discs in multiple systems reach lower maximum dust masses than discs around single stars

evidence.quote: Discs around single stars and stars in multiple systems have similar dust mass cumulative distributions up to 50 M$_{\oplus}$.

claims.hypothesis: Disc mass and size depend on the projected separation of the companion
claims.experiment: Dust mass and disc semi-major axis versus projected separation for resolved binaries
claims.result: Massive, big discs are found only around wide binaries (>100 au); unresolved low-mass discs are in close binaries below 150 au
claims.finding: Close companions truncate discs while wide companions have little effect

evidence.quote: Massive, big discs are only found around wide ($>$ 100 au) binary systems.

claims.hypothesis: Visual binaries strongly affect the general disc population of Ophiuchus
claims.experiment: Comparison of dust mass and size distributions of singles and multiples across the full ODISEA sample
claims.result: Differences appear only in the tails of the distributions
claims.finding: The effect of visual binaries is weak for the general, mostly small and low-mass, disc population

evidence.quote: we note that most discs in Ophiuchus are small and low-mass and the effect of visual binaries is likely to be much weaker in the general disc population.

claims.hypothesis: NIR AO imaging of ODISEA discs reveals previously unknown companions including sub-stellar ones
claims.experiment: L' band NACO and NIRC2 imaging of 147 new targets plus revisits of known binaries
claims.result: 20 new binaries and one triple detected; 9 companions of 30-50 MJup
claims.finding: The visual multiplicity of ODISEA is 18%, likely a lower bound

evidence.quote: We detect 20 new binary systems and one new triple system.

why_this_data.value: NACO and NIRC2 chosen for efficiency with short exposures and small overheads

evidence.quote: These two instruments were chosen for their efficiency in taking short exposures with small overheads.

why_this_method.value: N90C10 AO configuration chosen for stable AO on faint targets

evidence.quote: Given the faintness of our targets, we chose the AO configuration N90C10 which provides NAOS with 90% of the stars light and the detector with the remaining 10%.

limitations_admitted.value: Observed multiplicity rate is biased because only members with discs are included

evidence.quote: Notice that this rate is biased by the fact that, in ODISEA, only Ophiuchus members with discs are included.

limitations_admitted.value: Multiplicity census incomplete for separations below 10 au and for diskless stars

evidence.quote: the multiplicity census in Ophiuchus is very incomplete for separations smaller than 10 au and for diskless stars.

limitations_admitted.value: Deconvolved disc sizes below the beam must be interpreted with caution

evidence.quote: However, we emphasize that the deconvolved disc sizes must be interpreted with caution.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust masses use a single flux conversion (0.58 Earth masses per mJy at 140 pc, 20 K) for all stellar masses and no optical depth correction
Two ALMA samples have very different resolution and sensitivity, so categories mix detection biases
Companion flux ratio detection thresholds were not quantified per target
Stellar mass dependence of disc mass is not controlled when comparing singles and binaries

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small for the NIR images; the ALMA part uses published fluxes (ALMA ODISEA Cycle-4 continuum, tens of GB if re-imaged)
reproducibility.score_reason: Observing programs and project code are given, the dust-mass recipe is simple, and the binary table is printed, but ALMA reduction is deferred to other papers and the NIR companion photometry and filter settings are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA reduction and source fluxes live in other papers, and the main results are mostly counts and distribution comparisons rather than fitted numeric values.
